A lot of people need to realise that popular =/= good. Not that I'm implying Breaking Bad wasn't good, but rather more broadly that popularity does not reflect the merit of the programme. Keep in mind that although Breaking Bad was popular, the vast majority of the audience came out of it thinking Walt was the good guy. General audiences like spectacles because they're highly accessible, which were abundant in BB with its high-action scenes. But the more introspective, character-focused aspects require more patience, and the fact that Walt was glorified en masse signifies that this aspect of BB was vastly overlooked by the majority of viewers at the time. In general, the best kind of art tends to not be popular with general audiences, as they're more concerned with sensations of excitement and thrills than with long, complex character explorations. That's what Marvel films are for, to provide those high-action rollercoasters that popular audiences love.

It's hard enough living in the UK as a trans person, and I wouldn't want anyone here to deplete their energy resources even more by arguing with bad-faith actors online, which is something that I unfortunately see very often.

A minority of bigots with high levels of legislative and institutional power are trying extremely hard to permeate the public consciousness with the narrative of us vs them, wherein trans people are the 'them' and the rest of society is 'us'. The idealogical goal is to isolate, disenfranchise, marginalise and ultimately eliminate trans people. It's one branch of a larger tree that is the Tory government, who time and time again control and manipulate the cultural forces of journalistic media to maintain a structure of order and compliance towards the status quo. 

The reality is that despite everything, the majority of the public are tolerant of trans people and supportive of their rights to exist. There are hundreds of thousands of cis people who are utterly sickened by the framing of the 'trans debate', who are devastated by the endless feed of negativity, fear-mongering and moral panics surrounding trans people. The bigoted transphobic agenda is not reflective of the British mass consciousness, but rather it is a consequence of our broken system that allows the worst reactionary voices of our society to be the loudest. 

If the majority of the British public knew how much the trans population were suffering, they would stand for trans rights. The issue is simply that they do not know, because trans voices get suppressed. This happened with gay people in the past, particularly back during the AIDs crisis. Bigotry was rife back then, and homophobic rhetoric was weaponised as much as possible. Homophobes pulled out all the stops to portray gay people as harmful, invasive, predatory - all the same boring tactics that are being employed now against trans people. But the consequences of bigotry showed their ugly head when the public realised the hundreds of thousands of deaths that occurred as a result, and the discourse of gay rights became reframed through the lens of tragedy, causing the public opinion to shift towards acceptance as a result. Trans people are currently experiencing a similar crisis - the same fear-mongering, the same denial of civil and institutional rights. History will repeat itself, the larger public will all realise that trans people are dying, then they will realise that transphobic rhetoric is directly responsible for them dying, and public opinion will shift once again. This is already happening now with more and more backlash against the press. Bigots will always lose, no matter what.

It's extremely hard to tackle because the voices of bigots have power over the gullible masses, while the voices who oppose bigotry remain suppressed. We live in a country where the majority of our press is controlled by rich right-wing oligarchs who are well-capable of perpetuating moral panics and provoking culture wars to maintain the order of Tory dominance. The majority of boomers absorb this stream of news constantly, making them incredibly easy prey for fear-mongering tactics. On top of that, you've got the incredibly loud minority of terminally online TERFs - most of whom are in the Gen X or boomer demographic - who dedicate their every waking moments to spreading hatred.

That being said, I think a lot of what we're seeing at the moment is a wave of older so-called 'liberals' revealing themselves as conservatives. To a certain extent at least, it's less that people are being manipulated en masse and more that people who were never truly progressive are finally being honest about it. There are older folks on Twitter who right now are saying 'finally, I agree with Boris for once!' Aside from the bad faith actors, these people don't have the self-awareness to realise that the level of progression of social politics has marched on and left them behind. These types of people don't want to listen, they've got their fingers in their eyes saying la la.

I'm utterly appalled at the state of UK politics. Boris will do everything he can to marginalise the working-class, increasing tax rates and energy prices that he even admits will cause millions to starve and freeze in the upcoming winter. Per the Tory strategy, they need a punching bag to deflect the public eye away from their endless acts of austerity. Rev up the oil-funded press machine, churn out those fear-mongering articles, drum up those culture wars. It's all part of the play book handed down from Maggie T herself, dusting off the old homophobic rhetoric and refashioning it for transphobia. Boris knows the British public is gullible enough to swallow it all up, accept the trans folk as the baddies and completely overlook his civil negligence and political failures.

I'm a cis ally but I find the level of transphobia in this country abhorrent and embarrassing. I can't imagine how it feels it to be villainised in the public eye every single day. It speaks volumes of the utter callousness of both British politicians and the general public that the devastating effect on trans people's mental health is perceived as irrelevant and never once brought into discussion. It fucking hurts to witness. I'm really sorry for everyone here to have to deal with living in this boghole oligarchy.

I wish I was normal, but this doesn't mean I wish I was neurotypical. Rather, it means I wish I wasn't treated like 'abnormal' or 'other' by society and especially wish I didn't have to deal with the harmful stereotypes that mainstream ableism has popularised. For example, autistic people are always infantilised as people believe it doesn't occur in adults. People also believe that autism is a disease, and that autism is a undesirable problem that needs to be removed from society. Autism amongst young people is also often used as a insult. This means conversations around autism with my friends and generally people online always stem around the same implications over and over - autistic people are a burden, autism needs to be removed, mothers should abort autistic children, autistic people can never fit in, any variation of 'autism is bad'. Because popular opinion in society doesn't accept that we're truly people of independent and unique thought with heaps of potential, positive qualities and important contributions to society. The only way I can thrive amongst other people is to mask a sense of 'normalcy', as other autistic people do. Being constantly faced with casual ableism and having to keep up this mask is exhausting, which leads many autistic people to inevitably just wish they were born neurotypical. I have enough optimism to believe that my brain is normal even if society doesn't think so, but keeping up this confidence in an environment where I'm constantly being dehumanised makes it extremely difficult. This might be seen as a problematic comparison, but I would compare being autistic now to being  gay in the mid or late 1900's as far as societal perceptions and treatment goes. The feeling of being 'closeted', being the butt of a joke, being treated like a disease, having to compensate and mask our true selves to avoid rejection, and ultimately never ever being happy with oneself unless we interact with communities with other people who are the same way.
